title: Chapter 86 — The Delivered Base: Repeat Business & The Replacement Cycle
intro: Replacement-cycle timing, base mining, and lifetime-value arithmetic.

sections.title: The Replacement Cycle
sections.content:
Appliances have predictable lifespans. Refrigerators: 12-15 years. Dishwashers: 10-12 years. Ranges: 15-20 years. Washers and dryers: 10-12 years.

Every customer in your delivered base will need new appliances on a predictable schedule. If you sold a family a fridge in 2020, they will need a dishwasher around 2025 and a washer/dryer around 2027. That is three more sales from one relationship — if you maintain it.

sections.title: Base Mining
sections.content:
Your delivered base is your most valuable asset. These customers already trust you. They already know your store. They already had a positive experience. Selling to them costs almost nothing compared to acquiring a new customer.

The proactive touch: 'Hi [name], it has been a year since we set up your dishwasher. How is everything running? If you are thinking about any other upgrades, I am here whenever you are ready.'

That call takes 90 seconds and it keeps you top of mind for the next appliance purchase.

sections.title: Lifetime Value Math
sections.content:
A single customer who buys from you at 35 will need approximately $15,000-25,000 in appliances over their lifetime. Plus their referrals — conservatively 5-10 people, each worth $3,000-8,000.

One well-maintained customer relationship is worth $30,000-80,000 in lifetime revenue. That is why the 48-hour follow-up call, the annual check-in, and the referral ask matter so much. You are not being nice. You are investing in a compounding asset.
